rows.subtopic: Telling the truth after a mistake
rows.subtype: Approach: learning a rule from the mistake [Revision]
rows.description: After being honest about forgetting to feed the birds, a girl sets a phone reminder for her mother and puts the seed box near the window so it does not happen again.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, mental simulation, trial by imitation

rows.description: When a friend asks to copy the maths answers, a girl says no and offers to explain the method after class instead, holding firm without ending the friendship.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: mental simulation, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: thinking of what the test is for [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy reasons that copying gives marks but no learning, and that he would be lost in the next chapter, so helping someone cheat does not truly help them.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, mental simulation, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: giving in to keep the friendship [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child shows his answers because he fears the friend will stop talking to him, and worries afterwards, since the teacher may blame both and the fear kept growing.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, mental simulation, seeking advice

rows.description: A girl suggests studying together on Sunday, so her friend can prepare properly, which meets the friend's real need of not failing without breaking the rules.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, mental simulation, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: telling the teacher when the friend will not stop [Revision]
rows.description: After saying no twice, a boy learns that the friend plans to bring a chit into the exam, so he speaks privately with the teacher, thinking that stopping a bigger problem is worth it.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, mental simulation, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: thinking that everyone does it [Pitfall]
rows.description: A girl tells herself that half the class copies so it is normal, but when caught during a test she finds that a common habit is still against the rule and still has consequences.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, mental simulation, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: rehearsing a light reply to avoid a fight [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy prepares to say that he does not want trouble with the teacher, a reason that sounds about himself rather than judging the friend, making refusal easier to accept.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: tempted by fear of failing [Thinking]
rows.description: A child who is afraid of low marks feels the pull to peek at a neighbour's page, and recognises that fear is what makes cheating tempting, so he asks his teacher for extra help.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, mental simulation

rows.subtype: Approach: asking a parent what to do about a friend [Action]
rows.description: A girl unsure whether telling on a friend is right talks it over with her mother, who helps her see how to be kind and honest at the same time.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, mental simulation
